description: Checks that a monthly-rated employee's agreed salary is at least the RM1,700 monthly minimum wage.

references.title: Minimum Wages Order 2024 [P.U.(A) 376/2024] paras 2, 3(1), 5(1)
references.locator: RM1,700 a month for a monthly-rated employee; para 2 leaves out only a domestic employee as EA s.2(1) defines one. An apprentice is inside: the National Wages Consultative Council (Amendment) Act 2025 brought apprenticeship contracts into Act 732 from 1 August 2025.

description: Checks that a part-time employee's agreed rate, converted to an hourly equivalent, meets the RM8.72 hourly minimum.

references.title: Minimum Wages Order 2024 [P.U.(A) 376/2024] paras 3(1), 5(1)
references.locator: RM8.72 an hour, including a part-time employee's rate derived from the agreed month, week or day.

references.title: Employment (Part-Time Employees) Regulations 2010 [P.U.(A) 302/2010]
references.locator: the part-time hourly rate is the agreed rate divided by the agreed normal hours.

description: Rejects a Sabah or Sarawak worksite, which is governed by its own Labour Ordinance rather than the Employment Act.

references.title: Employment Act 1955 (Act 265) First Schedule
references.locator: the Act governs Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan.

references.title: Labour Ordinance (Sabah) Cap. 67; Labour Ordinance (Sarawak) Cap. 76
references.locator: a Sabah or Sarawak worksite is governed by its own Ordinance, which this lineage does not encode.

description: Checks that agreed normal weekly hours do not exceed 45, except for shift work averaged over three weeks.

references.title: Employment Act 1955 s.60A(1)(d)
references.locator: the normal hours of work may not exceed 45 in one week.

references.title: Employment Act 1955 s.60C(1)
references.locator: shift work may average the normal hours over three weeks.

description: Checks that a daily-rated employee's agreed rate meets the daily minimum wage for a four-, five- or six-day week.

references.title: Minimum Wages Order 2024 [P.U.(A) 376/2024] paras 3(1), 5(1)
references.locator: RM98.08, RM78.46 and RM65.38 a day for a four-, five- and six-day week.

description: Checks that an hourly-rated employee's agreed rate is at least RM8.72 an hour.

references.title: Minimum Wages Order 2024 [P.U.(A) 376/2024] paras 3(1), 5(1)
references.locator: RM8.72 an hour.

description: Requires wages to be paid into the employee's bank account unless a non-bank method has the Director General's approval.

references.title: Employment Act 1955 (Act 265)
references.locator: s.25A
references.quote: Wages are paid through a bank account opened in the employee's name unless the employee makes a written request for another method; payment in cash or by cheque needs the Director General's approval.

description: Checks that the employer's payment schedule does not cover more than one month.

references.title: Employment Act 1955 s.18
references.locator: a wage period may not exceed one month.

description: Requires a thirty-minute break in planned overtime that would run more than five consecutive hours, judged on the breaks each span records.

references.title: Employment Act 1955 s.60A(1)(a) and proviso (i)
references.locator: no more than five consecutive hours without a period of leisure of not less than thirty minutes; a break of less than thirty minutes does not break the continuity of the five hours.

description: Checks that the rostered shift and its planned overtime do not take a day beyond twelve hours of work, and that a month's overtime on working or off days stays within the statutory cap; rest-day work is outside that cap.

references.title: Employment Act 1955 s.60A(7) and s.60C(2)
references.locator: except in the emergencies of s.60A(2)(a) to (e), no employer shall require any employee to work for more than twelve hours in any one day, overtime and rest-day work included.

references.title: Employment Act 1955 s.60A(9)
references.locator: hours of work: the time the employee is at the disposal of the employer; an unpaid break is not.

references.title: Employment Act 1955 s.60A(4)(a); Employment (Limitation of Overtime Work) Regulations 1980 reg.2
references.locator: overtime is limited to one hundred and four hours in any one month. The proviso in s.60A(4)(a) leaves work on a rest day or a gazetted public holiday out of the cap, though it is still paid at the rest-day and holiday rates. Off days are not that statutory rest day, so their hours count.

description: Requires a permitted employment category for a worker under fifteen.

references.title: Children and Young Persons (Employment) Act 1966 (Act 350) s.2(2)
references.locator: a child under fifteen may work only in light family work, licensed public entertainment, school-approved work or an approved apprenticeship.

description: Requires a worker doing light family work to be at least thirteen.

references.title: Children and Young Persons (Employment) Act 1966 (Act 350) s.2(2A)
references.locator: light work in a family undertaking requires age thirteen or above.

description: Prohibits hazardous work for a child and requires personal supervision and training for a young person.

references.title: Children and Young Persons (Employment) Act 1966 (Act 350) s.2(1A)–(1B), Fourth Schedule
references.locator: hazardous work is prohibited for a child; a young person needs personal supervision and an apprenticeship or vocational training.

description: Prohibits Fifth Schedule employment for anyone under eighteen.

references.title: Children and Young Persons (Employment) Act 1966 (Act 350) s.2(2B), Fifth Schedule
references.locator: Fifth Schedule employment is prohibited for every person under eighteen; training does not exempt it.

description: Restricts the contract's statutory work category and residency status to the values this jurisdiction recognises.

references.title: Employment Act 1955 First Schedule (as amended by Act A1651, 1 January 2023)
references.locator: the statutory work category fixes coverage and the overtime, rest-day and holiday premia.

references.title: Employment Act 1955 s.2(1) "domestic employee"; EPF Act 1991 First Schedule para (2)
references.locator: DOMESTIC
references.quote: Work of a private dwelling-house, not of a trade, business or profession carried on by the employer. EPF para (2) keeps a domestic servant of a registered business, society or corporation in the Fund: such a person is not this category.

description: Checks the recorded worksite region and annual-leave carry limit against the jurisdiction's declared bounds.

references.title: Employment Act 1955 First Schedule
references.locator: the recorded worksite region must be one this lineage governs.

references.title: Agreed annual-leave carry
references.locator: the contract may not agree a negative carry limit.

description: Requires a sealed employer that is HRD-compulsory or not registered to record the date its registration liability began.

references.title: Pembangunan Sumber Manusia Berhad Act 2001 (Act 612) s.4 and First Schedule
references.locator: a compulsory employer's registration liability runs from the actual date it began.

description: Requires a death, departure or non-bank wage case to name the employment and carry its source document.

references.title: Employment Act 1955 s.25A
references.locator: a non-bank wage request is the employee's signed writing, not an employer note.

references.title: Income Tax Act 1967 (Act 53) s.83(4)
references.locator: a departure from Malaysia needs the actual expected departure and its CP21 review.

description: Requires a non-bank wage request to carry the employee's signed request, dated on or before the case was opened.

references.title: Employment Act 1955 s.25A(1)
references.locator: cash or cheque payment needs the employee's written request, signed before it takes effect.

description: Requires an overseas departure case to record the actual expected departure date and any later return date.

references.title: Income Tax Act 1967 (Act 53) s.83(4)–(5)
references.locator: the employer gives CP21 notice before the actual departure; a known ordered return date cannot precede it.

description: Checks that the employer's recorded notice of death does not precede the death.

references.title: Employment Act 1955 s.19–21
references.locator: the employer's notice of the employee's death starts the final-wage duty; it cannot precede the recorded death.

description: Applies the annual-leave service rules for unauthorised absence and more than thirty days of unpaid leave in a year.

references.title: Employment Act 1955 (Act 265) s.60E(1), second proviso
references.locator: absence without permission and without reasonable excuse on more than ten per cent of the working days of the twelve months: no such leave.

references.title: Employment Act 1955 (Act 265) s.60E(3B)
references.locator: leave of absence without pay exceeding thirty days in the aggregate in any twelve months is disregarded in computing the length of service.

description: Requires twelve months' continuous service before paternity leave begins.

references.title: Employment Act 1955 (Act 265) s.60FA(3)(a)
references.locator: employed by the same employer at least twelve months immediately before the commencement of the paternity leave.
